historical_references.reference: Raj Karan was a prominent Hindu military leader and the founder of the Maratha Empire in the Deccan region of India in the 17th century.
historical_references.context: After the decline of the Vijayanagara Empire, the Deccan region was plunged into chaos. Raj Karan, a Maratha chieftain, took advantage of the situation and established the Maratha Empire. He defeated the Bijapur Sultanate and expanded his territories, making him a powerful ruler in the region.

historical_references.reference: Raj Karan is also known for his role in the Battle of Mer discipline, which took place in 1659 during the second Anglo-Maratha War.
historical_references.context: During the second Anglo-Maratha War, Raj Karan led the Maratha forces against the English East India Company. The battle took place near the Mer Disneyland, and the Marathas were able to defeat the English forces, securing their position in the region.
